column1: # KiCad <-> IR layer projection — WORKING copy — edit me.
# This file is the shipped reference. The code operates on the WORKING copy
# (kicad_layers.tsv); if that is missing or unparseable, it falls back to
# THIS file. Do not edit the reference — edit the working copy.
# The layer mapping is a property of the KiCad importer/exporter, not of the
# IR, which is why it lives in data you can edit rather than in code.
# Columns (whitespace-separated):   IR   KiCad
#   IR    : IR layer number. When the KiCad name starts with "F.", the layer
#           is PAIRED and the code derives the bottom side automatically
#           (-IR <-> "B."+name). Standalone names (Edge.Cuts, *.User) have
#           no side.
#   KiCad : KiCad layer name (must exist in the board's (layers ...) table).
# ORDER MATTERS. Forward (IR->KiCad) uses every row. Reverse (KiCad->IR)
# uses the FIRST row that names a given KiCad layer, so list the canonical
# layer first and any collapsing aliases after it (e.g. 151 F.Fab is the
# real fab layer; 125/127 also render onto F.Fab but come back as 151).
# Any IR/KiCad layer NOT listed here is DROPPED on conversion (logged, never
# silent). To carry an extra layer: change its layer in the source, or add a
# row here.
# --- copper (inner layers In1.Cu.. are numbered from the stack, not here) ---
1     F.Cu
# --- silk / mask / paste / courtyard / fab ---
121   F.SilkS
129   F.Mask
131   F.Paste
139   F.CrtYd
151   F.Fab
125   F.Fab               # tNames  -> fab graphic (reverse F.Fab -> 151 above)
127   F.Fab               # tValues -> fab graphic
# --- board outline ---
120   Edge.Cuts
# --- side-less user / documentation layers (Eagle 47-50, IR 147-150) ---
147   Eco1.User           # Eagle 47 Measures
148   Cmts.User           # Eagle 48 Document
149   Eco2.User           # Eagle 49 Reference
150   Dwgs.User           # Eagle 50 dxf (canonical reverse for Dwgs.User)
146   Dwgs.User           # PLATING marker: no KiCad concept, a visible note
